style.fontFamily: "Microsoft JhengHei", "Noto Sans CJK TC", "PingFang TC", "Segoe UI", sans-serif

p02-c2-t.text:
The sign of the correction depends on both residual and feature: you cannot say 'positive error raises all weights'; a negative feature flips the direction
The general stochastic-approximation form: $\mathbf{w}_k=\mathbf{w}_{k-1}+\rho_kF(\mathbf{x}_k,\mathbf{w}_{k-1})$; LMS's $F=\mathbf{x}_k(y_k-\mathbf{x}_k^T\mathbf{w}_{k-1})$
One correction can be noisy; the path does not get closer to the goal at every step

p06-ctx-t.text: **Used on this page**: $\rho_k>0$, $\sum\rho_k=\infty$, $\sum\rho_k^2<\infty$; $1/k$ holds; mean stability $0<\rho<2/\lambda_{\max}(R_x)$.

p06-fig-title.name: p06-fig-title

style.fontFamily: "Microsoft JhengHei", "Noto Sans CJK TC", "PingFang TC", "Segoe UI", sans-serif

p06-fig-title.text: Myth check: step conditions are not a cure-all

p06-c2-t.name: p06-c2-t

style.fontFamily: "Microsoft JhengHei", "Noto Sans CJK TC", "PingFang TC", "Segoe UI", sans-serif

p06-c2-t.text:
Mean weight error: $E[\mathbf{w}_k-\mathbf{w}^\ast ]=(I-\rho R_x)E[\mathbf{w}_{k-1}-\mathbf{w}^\ast ]$; needs $0<\rho<2/\lambda_{\max}(R_x)$; the source's $2/\operatorname{tr}(R_x)$ is more conservative
[Added] Independent standard Gaussian, noiseless scalar model: mean-square factor $1-2\rho+3\rho^2$; needs $0<\rho<2/3$, stricter than the mean condition $0<\rho<2$
Mean stability is not mean-square stability, which also involves fourth moments

p06-ban-t.name: p06-ban-t

style.fontFamily: "Microsoft JhengHei", "Noto Sans CJK TC", "PingFang TC", "Segoe UI", sans-serif

p06-ban-t.text: Takeaway: mean stability is not mean-square stability; step conditions must come with data assumptions.
